terms.grammar: adverb; prīdiē quam with a clause, prīdiē ejus diēī, or prīdiē with the accusative of a date
evidence: Cic. Att. 5.11.6: prīdiē quam ego Athēnās vēnī (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 1.47: prīdiē ejus diēī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: One word for “on the day before”. Before an event it takes quam: prīdiē quam abīret, the day before he left; before a named day the accusative: prīdiē Kalendās. Its pair is postrīdiē, the day after.

phrases.latin: nēmō nostrum est īdem māne quī fuit prīdiē
phrases.english: none of us is the same in the morning as he was the day before
on the day before he left

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 86, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.: p. 300.
